sections.title: Portable Workflows As Source Code
sections.body: Codex Skills Library turns repeatable agent behavior into source-controlled folders rather than loose prompts or chat memory. The project keeps each skill portable with trigger metadata, instructions, references, scripts, examples, assets, and agent metadata, then uses generated catalogs to make the suite inspectable. The important decision is operational: workflows should be reusable and reviewable, but still checked inside the target repository where local instructions, constraints, and verification commands matter.

sections.title: Catalog Discipline And Human Review
sections.body: The repository separates skill membership, lifecycle metadata, generated catalog output, plugin backups, and public docs-site pages. Catalog scripts detect drift before regeneration, while the maintainer decides whether a local skill belongs in the curated suite or should stay outside the public catalog. That distinction matters because the repo is public-learning-oriented but still preserves provenance-sensitive skill folders, third-party notices, local plugin backups, and unresolved license boundaries.

sections.title: Current Intake Boundary
sections.body: This intake records the repo locally as a Hyphenomenon project without mutating the production knowledge database. The captured state includes a local docs-site review, source-backed hydration artifacts, and an explicit drift finding: an in-progress `hyphenomenon-chat-intake` skill folder exists outside `skills/SUITE_SKILLS.txt`. That is useful proof of the real operating model because the project depends on human/operator review before deciding whether local skill work becomes curated public catalog content.

productSurfaces.title: Skill Source Library
productSurfaces.summary: `skills/` contains portable custom Codex skill folders, with suite membership governed by `skills/SUITE_SKILLS.txt` and lifecycle metadata tracked separately.

productSurfaces.title: Plugin Backup Library
productSurfaces.summary: `plugins/` preserves selected custom local plugin bundles separately from the standalone skill suite so larger surfaces keep plugin metadata, assets, scripts, and bundled skills intact.

productSurfaces.title: Generated Public Docs Site
productSurfaces.summary: `docs-site/` is a Next.js catalog and documentation surface generated from source metadata so readers can browse skills and plugin patterns without hand-maintained marketing pages.

productSurfaces.title: Repo-Native Evidence And Project Memory
productSurfaces.summary: `DOCS/` stores lean notes, project memory, evidence, and intake artifacts for repository maintenance without turning the repo into a full delivery scaffold.

keyDates.note: Git history records a skills sync workflow repair, aligning with the durable convention that local Codex skills are reconciled into this repository through explicit checks.

dataModelHighlights.title: Skill Suite Catalog Model
dataModelHighlights.summary: The curated suite is modeled as a set of skill folders, an allowlist, lifecycle metadata, generated human-readable index, generated machine-readable manifest, and docs-site catalog data.

dataModelHighlights.title: Plugin Backup Model
dataModelHighlights.summary: Custom plugins are backed up as plugin folders with `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, assets/scripts, and registry metadata rather than being mixed into the standalone skill catalog.

dataModelHighlights.title: Workflow Verification Model
dataModelHighlights.summary: Repo maintenance relies on explicit preflight checks, generated catalog diffs, local docs-site review, and human/operator decisions before in-progress local skill work becomes curated public catalog content.

dataModels.title: Skill Suite Catalog Model
